title: Heavy lifting

brief.story: Three white LEDs (a strip segment) should come on with the button. This time the switch is a MOSFET: its gate needs a voltage, not a current. The gate resistor, the pull-down and the wiring are in; the MOSFET isn’t.
brief.goal: Fit the IRLZ44N in columns 10–12 so all three LEDs carry 15–20 mA while SW1 is held, and go dark when it’s let go.

datasheet.title: IRLZ44N · N-channel MOSFET
rows: from S to D: points backwards

hints: Click column 10 with the MOSFET: G lands in 10, D in 11, S in 12. The gate is driven from SW1, the LEDs’ cathodes are on column 11, and column 12 goes to ground.
G · D · S, left to right. Turned round (S in 10), its body diode connects the LEDs to ground and they never switch off.
With the gate at 9 V the MOSFET is a 0.03 Ω switch: each LED gets (9 − 3.0) ÷ 330 = 18 mA.

spec.explain: A MOSFET turns on when its gate is a couple of volts above its source; turned round, its body diode conducts all the time.

debrief: A MOSFET is switched by voltage: its gate is insulated, so it draws no current once charged, and when it’s on its channel is a fraction of an ohm. That’s why LED strips, motors and heaters are driven by MOSFETs. The 10 kΩ pull-down holds the gate low when the button is let go, and the pinout matters: backwards, the built-in body diode conducts.
